rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to observe all six compounds and identify the elution window and critical pairs. A midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.
The maximum CRF is already achieved, so shorten the gradient to seek a faster fully resolved method. Changing only tG also tests the slope sensitivity of the closest pair, currently at R = 2.68.

Test the next shorter gradient to locate the resolution limit for the critical pair. Injection 2 already retains the maximum CRF and provides a fully resolved fallback if this steeper gradient loses separation.

The critical pair loses resolution as the gradient steepens, making 8 minutes the shortest fully resolved gradient tested at 40 C. Test 60 C at the 6-minute gradient to determine whether temperature shifts selectivity enough to restore separation while shortening retention.
Test the opposite temperature extreme while holding the gradient fixed. Cooling may improve the critical middle-pair separation and avoids the early-pair co-elution seen at 60 C.

Return to the fully resolved 8-minute gradient and test moderate heating to shorten retention. The temperature scans suggest 50 C may improve the middle-pair separation without causing the early-pair co-elution observed at 60 C.

Trim the gradient window around the estimated peak elution range of 0.20–0.51 organic fraction. This preserves injection 6’s gradient slope while reducing the initial low-organic interval, testing whether full resolution can be maintained in a faster method.

Shift the gradient window upward by 0.05 while preserving its slope to reduce retention further. Check whether the early peaks remain sufficiently retained and the critical middle pair maintains R ≥ 1.5; injection 7 remains a maximum-score fallback.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness to recover the critical pair, which narrowly missed full resolution at R = 1.46. Keeping the higher starting organic fraction should retain much of injection 8’s time savings relative to injection 7.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step while keeping the endpoint fixed. This may shorten retention while the resulting shallower gradient offsets compression of the critical middle pair; monitor early-pair resolution as well.

Test a substantially steeper gradient to see whether the critical middle pair crosses elution order and regains separation on the other side. This explores a faster operating region while retaining injection 10 as the fastest fully resolved method tested.

Explore the reversed-order separation region using a higher starting organic fraction and lower temperature. Cooling should help retain and separate the early peaks, while the narrower gradient window reduces compression relative to injection 11.

Shift injection 12’s window upward while preserving its slope to test whether starting-solvent selectivity can improve the unresolved middle pair. The early pair has substantial resolution margin, although its retention and separation must be checked at this higher starting organic fraction.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction and shallower gradient can bring the reversed middle pair to baseline resolution. This is exploratory: the first peak is already nearly unretained, so early-pair compression is a risk; injection 10 remains the fastest fully resolved fallback.

Reduce the gradient slope at the same starting composition and temperature to spread the critical middle pair, now at R = 1.22. The early pair has some margin at R = 2.43, and the stronger late retention should still leave the final peak well within 10 minutes.

The critical pair barely improved when the gradient was made shallower, so test temperature-dependent selectivity instead. A 5 C increase relative to injection 14 probes whether this fast operating region can reach full resolution without exhausting the early pair’s separation margin.

Return near the fastest fully resolved method, injection 10, and test a shorter gradient with a lower endpoint. This modestly increases slope and moves late peaks into the hold, testing whether the critical middle pair remains resolved while reducing total elution time.

Refine the maximum-score region by making injection 9’s gradient one step shallower. This should increase the critical middle-pair margin while retaining adequate early-pair separation and keeping the final peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step from injection 18 to shorten retention while preserving a shallower slope than injection 10. This tests a compromise between injection 10’s speed and injection 18’s resolution margin.

Test a 5 C reduction from injection 19 to improve the limiting early-pair separation while checking that the middle pair retains its resolution margin. This probes a nearby maximum-score method with more balanced separation; injection 10 remains the fastest fully resolved method tested.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step from injection 20 to shorten retention, using its improved early-pair separation as margin. The shallower gradient may help preserve middle-pair resolution, though both critical pairs need checking.

Return to the proven lower-starting-organic region and test injection 9’s gradient at 45 C. Modest cooling should improve early-pair separation while potentially retaining full middle-pair resolution, giving another maximum-score option near the fastest successful methods.

Test the fastest fully resolved gradient from injection 10 at 45 C to improve its early-pair margin. Injection 20 suggests the middle pair may tolerate this modest cooling, although its resolution is likely to remain close to the 1.5 threshold.

Combine injection 18’s shallower gradient with moderate cooling to seek a maximum-score method with greater separation margin than the fastest method. The neighboring results suggest both critical pairs should remain above R = 1.5, with the last peak comfortably within 10 minutes.

Use the final injection to test a shallower variant of injection 7, aiming to preserve maximum CRF with greater critical-pair separation and adequate early retention. The maximum possible score is already secured; injection 10 remains the fastest fully resolved method tested.
